skill1: Refresh Heart: Incoming healing ▲ 6.53%, stacks up to 5 time(s) and lasts for 15 sec. (no incoming-healing StatKey; no HP pool modeled — tracked only as the named stack the burst heal gates on)
Restores HP equal to 4.45% of the skill user's final Max HP. (HP amount not modeled; the recovery EVENT is emitted so teammate on-recovery triggers fire)
skill2: ATK ▼ 3.55% for 5 sec. (enemy ATK debuff — boss damage is unmodeled at scope lock, so this is inert)
burst: Increases stack count of stackable buffs by 1. (no schema primitive for incrementing an arbitrary already-applied buff's stack count — engine has no cross-buff stack-bump effect)
Activates when Refresh Heart is at max stacks. (stack-count gate not expressible — no resourceGate on a named ally buff; modeled as unconditional, see caveats)
Restores HP equal to 27.22% of the skill user's final Max HP. (HP amount not modeled; recovery event only)

caveats: ⛑ skill2 trigger + cadence INVENTED: the kit line carries no activation clause, so it is modeled as interval/20s from the datamined skill cooldown. Both the kind (interval vs an event trigger) and the 20s are unmeasured.
⛑ skill2 first-fire phase is the t=sec convention (first hit at 20s, not t=0) — not a kit-stated or measured value.

⛑ burst 27.22% heal is gated in-kit on Refresh Heart at MAX (5) stacks; that gate is not modeled, so the recovery event fires on every burst cast. Refresh Heart gains 1 stack per last-bullet (one per 9-round magazine), so at a real cadence max stacks is plausibly reached before the first burst — but whether it holds at cast time (15s stack duration vs magazine cadence) is unverified. If it does NOT hold, this over-fires teammates' on-recovery triggers.
⛑ The 'increases stack count of stackable buffs by 1' line is dropped entirely. If it lands on a teammate's damage-relevant stacking buff, the model UNDER-credits the team.
⛑ Both damage lines are written noRange (function damage takes no +30% range bonus). Burst-cast damage is noFb per the pre-FB rule; the skill2 rider keeps FB-by-timing (default ON).

⛑ Cadence tuple (SG 9 ammo / 142 reloadFrames / 10 hitsPerShot) is datamined and drives last-bullet frequency, which is the ONLY thing making skill1 fire — an ammo/reload error moves both heal and stack cadence.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⛑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. pepper is an SG/Wind/Supporter/Burst-I healer with almost no self-damage surface: her only damage is skill2's 160% rider and the burst's 1237.5% hit, both single-target function damage on the highest-ATK enemy (one boss at scope lock, so the targeting clause is a no-op). Her sim-relevant output is therefore (a) two damage instances and (b) recovery EVENTS that fire teammates' 'recovery' triggers — heals are modeled as events with no HP amount, per the engine's no-HP-pool scope. Refresh Heart (incoming healing ▲) has no StatKey and no consumer while HP is unmodeled; it is carried in unmodeled, not as a buff block. The empty-effects allies block on skill1 is retained ONLY to keep the audit 1:1 with the kit's two ■ headers — it applies nothing.

flags.reasoning: The skill2 damage line carries NO activation clause, which per the trigger-identity taxonomy classifies it as an interval trigger rather than an event trigger. The 20s comes from the unit's datamined skill cooldown — the only cadence number available — not from the kit text, which states no period at all. This is the single largest uncertainty in the override: it sets how many times the 160% rider fires across a 180s fight (9 at 20s, ~18 at 10s), i.e. it linearly scales her entire non-burst damage contribution.
flags.recipe: Focus-record pepper in a fight and count the 160% popups across the 180s window; the popup interval IS the cadence. Cross-check the popup VALUE against 160% × her final ATK to confirm the line is the one firing (SG normal-attack pellets read very differently). If popups arrive at a non-uniform spacing, the trigger is an EVENT trigger (most likely lastBullet, since her whole kit keys off it) and this block must be re-keyed rather than re-timed.

flags.estimate: first fire at t=20s (the t=sec convention), not t=0
flags.reasoning: The engine's interval trigger fires first at t=sec. Whether a kit-silent recurring line actually fires once immediately at battle start is a convention, not a measurement, and over a 180s fight the choice is worth one whole activation (~11% of this line's total).
flags.recipe: Same focus recording: note whether a 160% popup appears in the opening seconds. Resolve together with the cadence flag above — one recording answers both.

flags.estimate: modeled UNGATED — fires on every burst cast
flags.reasoning: Refresh Heart accrues 1 stack per last-bullet, i.e. one per 9-round magazine, and needs 5 stacks with a 15s per-stack duration. Whether the pool actually sits at 5 when her burst casts depends on her real magazine cadence vs the 15s expiry, and on reload timing — none of which is measured. Because heals are event-only in v1, an over-firing gate does not create damage directly; it can only over-fire a TEAMMATE's 'recovery' trigger (a genuine damage path for on-recovery kits). I model it ON rather than OFF because 5 magazines is a low bar for a 9-round SG over 180s, but this is an estimate, not a derivation.
flags.recipe: Run her in a comp with an on-recovery consumer and compare that consumer's proc count against a run with this block removed; separately, count her reload cycles on a focus recording to establish whether 5 magazines complete inside any rolling 15s window before the first burst. If stacks do NOT hold at 5, the correct model is to drop this block entirely (no primitive can express the gate) and record it in unmodeled.

flags.reasoning: The line increments the stack count of ALL stackable buffs on all allies by 1. There is no effect kind that mutates a foreign, already-applied buff's stack count. If a teammate carries a damage-relevant stacking buff (ATK▲/crit▲ per stack), this drop UNDER-credits the team by roughly one stack's worth per pepper burst — potentially the most damage-relevant line in her entire kit, and it is the one line the schema cannot express.
flags.recipe: Not resolvable by measuring pepper alone. Pair her with a known per-stack damage buffer, focus that buffer, and compare its buff-stack readout (or its damage) with and without pepper's burst. If the effect is real and sizable, it is an ENGINE primitive request (a 'bumpStacks' effect), not an override fix — report it rather than approximating it with an invented flat buff.

flags.estimate: SG 9 ammo / 142 reloadFrames / 10 hitsPerShot, all datamined
flags.reasoning: lastBullet frequency is the sole clock for BOTH skill1 blocks, so ammo and reloadFrames — both known-unreliable datamine fields per the ALWAYS-⛑ taxonomy — set how often she heals and how fast Refresh Heart stacks. An ammo error propagates into the burst-heal gate question above.
flags.recipe: Read her ammo counter on a focus recording to confirm the 9-round magazine and time a full reload cycle in frames. This is the standard cadence-tuple measurement; no new instrument needed.

flags.estimate: alliesLowestHp count 1 → resolves to the leftmost ally
flags.reasoning: v1 models no HP pool (immortal boss, nobody takes damage), so 'lowest HP percentage' is indeterminate and the engine resolves it deterministically to the leftmost ally. Since the heal carries no HP amount and only emits a recovery event, WHICH ally receives it does matter for on-recovery consumers — a leftmost-slot consumer gets every proc, a rightmost one gets none.
flags.recipe: No in-game measurement can resolve this while HP is unmodeled — it is a scope limitation, not an unknown. If an on-recovery teammate's proc count is being validated against footage, note that slot order drives it and place the consumer accordingly, or treat the pairing as out of scope.
